title: Driven square lattice of quantum dots in a magnetic field coupled to a cylindrical FIR-photon cavity
authors: Vidar Gudmundsson, Vram Mughnetsyan, Hsi-Sheng Goan, Jeng-Da Chai, Nzar Rauf Abdullah, Chi-Shung Tang, Wen-Hsuan Kuan, Valeriu Moldoveanu, Andrei Manolescu
abstract: We present a comprehensive computational study of driven quantum dot arrays in a square lattice configuration, subject to an external magnetic field and coupled to a cylindrical far-infrared photon cavity. The driving is introduced through a harmonic modulation of the full electron-photon interaction, therefore including both paramagnetic and diamagnetic contributions. The electron-electron Coulomb interactions are treated within density functional theory, while the electron-photon coupling is modeled using a many-body configuration interaction approach at each iteration of the density functional. By exploiting the unique properties of the cylindrical TE$_{011}$ cavity mode, we demonstrate selective enhancement of diamagnetic two-photon transitions. Our results reveal that the effectiveness of harmonic modulation of the electron-photon interaction is strongly dependent on both the driving frequency and the electron occupation number per dot. When the driving frequency approaches twice the cavity photon frequency, the system exhibits resonant behavior characterized by efficient photon pumping, occupation of higher-order photon replicas, and activation of collective radial Coulomb breathing modes. These findings establish a controllable mechanism for manipulating photon states in coupled quantum dot-cavity systems and provide insights into the interplay among harmonic modulation, photonic excitations, magnetic confinement, and many-body electron correlations in dimensionally reduced nanostructures.
summary: This computational study analyzes driven quantum dot arrays coupled to an FIR photon cavity under a magnetic field. By applying harmonic modulation to the electron-photon interaction, the researchers demonstrate that resonant driving conditions allow for efficient pumping of photons and the excitation of collective electronic modes. This establishes a controllable platform for manipulating photonic states in nanostructures.
main_problem: The study investigates how driving a quantum dot array coupled to an FIR photon cavity can manipulate photonic states by controlling the interplay between harmonic modulation, magnetic confinement, and electron-photon interactions.
main_result: The system exhibits resonant behavior when the driving frequency approaches twice the cavity photon frequency, enabling efficient photon pumping and activating collective radial Coulomb breathing modes.
method: The research employs a Quantum Electrodynamical Density Functional Theory (QED-DFT-TP) approach solved via time evolution equations in a tensor product basis.
model_or_system: The system models a 2DEG confined in a square lattice of quantum dots, subjected to an external magnetic field and coupled to a cylindrical FIR photon cavity mode. The Hamiltonian includes electron kinetic/interaction terms, the cavity photon term, and a time-dependent modulation term applied to the electron-photon coupling.
key_observables: Mean photon number ($N_\gamma(t)$), dynamical orbital magnetization ($Q_J(t)$), collective radial Coulomb breathing modes, and energy spectrum showing 'photon replica bands'.
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\omega_{ext}$), cavity photon frequency ($\omega_\gamma$), electron occupation number per dot, and magnetic field strength (e.g., $B = 0.4138 	ext{ T}$).
main_assumptions: The TE$_{011}$ cavity mode is utilized; the calculation treats electron-electron interactions via DFT and models electron-photon coupling using a many-body configuration interaction approach.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy bandstructures showing photon replica bands, mean photon content mapping, and time evolution plots of $N_\gamma$ and collective oscillation diagnostics ($Q_0$, $Q_J$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the full Hamiltonian (including external modulation) to solving the dynamics using QED-DFT-TP. Key analyses focus on identifying resonant driving conditions that maximize photon pumping and observing resulting collective electronic excitations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines cavity QED principles with many-body physics in low-dimensional systems, providing a controllable mechanism for manipulating photons using external driving fields—a core theme in advanced AMO research.

Spintronics.note: The study models a system involving quantum dots (electron spins/states) coupled to an FIR photon cavity under a magnetic field, directly overlapping with the concept of hybrid spin-photon systems and cavity QED in magnets.
